target_customer: Hardware engineering teams in aerospace, energy, automotive and manufacturing that test engines, batteries, valves and plants
problem: Hardware teams stitch together LabVIEW, a time-series database and dashboards, which causes missed failures and slow test review.
business_model: Software platform with free desktop download and paid enterprise offering; pricing not found
product_category: Hardware control, data acquisition and test observability software

founders.name: Emiliano Bonilla
founders.background_notes: Per YC page: led data processing tools for early Firefly Alpha launches and worked on autonomous EV prototypes.

founders.name: Patrick Dotson
founders.background_notes: Per YC page: propulsion work on Starship.

founders.name: Elham Islam
founders.background_notes: Per YC page: flight software for Mars Sample Return Lander.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needs a high-rate time-series storage engine, drivers for industrial protocols such as OPC UA, Modbus and EtherCAT, and a real-time control layer, which is hard for a five person team.

defensibility.rationale: Once wired into a test stand and its data, teams rarely switch; but open components and a well-known incumbent leave room for copying.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows incumbents copying or buying Synnax.

market_need_then: Founders saw outdated control software and poor data review lead to costly hardware failures; the founders were the first beta users on a university rocketry team per YC.

branding.domain_note: Uses synnaxlabs.com with a Labs suffix, not the bare name.
branding.community_and_virality: Public GitHub repository; no merch or press about the brand found.

brand_strength.rationale: Distinctive but easily confused with syntax and other Synnax entities; niche audience and no brand press found.

outcome_analysis: Synnax is an active five person company from YC Summer 2024 whose founders come from SpaceX, NASA JPL and Firefly, which gives strong domain fit for aerospace test teams. No verified funding, exit or shutdown was found, so the outcome is undetermined. Its path depends on displacing entrenched LabVIEW workflows.
notes: Funding unverified and mixed with other companies named Synnax: aggregators give 500K to 1.5M and investors such as TON Ventures that likely belong to a different Synnax. Treat all as unverified. The only competitor named is from the YC description, undated. YC lists Denver; one aggregator lists San Francisco. Undated competitors left out of the list: LabVIEW (National Instruments).
